case_name: Durga Burman (Roy) v State of Sikkim
respondent:
State of Sikkim
Supreme Court of India

31 July 2014
Cr.A. No. 1010 of 2004
The Judgment was delivered by : Kurian Joseph, J.
1. Appellant is the second accused in Criminal Case No. 31 of 2001 on the file of the Sessions Judge, Sikkim at Gangtok. facts: The Appellant is the second accused in Criminal Case No. 31 of 2001 on the file of the Sessions Judge, Sikkim at Gangtok.

According to the prosecution: These two accused persons were already in need of money for their expenses as Durga Roy (Burman) had already borrowed much cash from his master Sujit Basak before completing his works and he had nothing to get from his master for few days.

The money problem became more serious when on 5.7.2001 the accused person received telephonic call from the father of Ranjit Roy stating that his mother is seriously ill at home and he should return home immediately.
That night both the accused persons slept late discussing about their monetary problems.
Next day (i.e. 6.7.2001) in the morning, Ranjit Roy went to the rented room.
Shibu Barman had already left for his job.
After some time Durga Roy (Barman) also arrived in the room.
Both of them were under the strong impression that Lalan Prasad had enough money in his house as he was engaged in lottery business and both his sons were also working.
issues: Whether the prosecution has been able to prove its case against the Appellant beyond reasonable doubt?
Whether the Appellant is guilty of offences punishable u/ss. 302 and 380 IPC?
court_reasoning: The court held that the prosecution has not laid any evidence on the score of common intention.
The court held that there is no legal bar to convict the Appellant under the substantive provision if on the basis of evidence it could be held that he was the author of the crime.
The court concluded that the Appellant after committing murder of the deceased, also committed theft of the wrist watch and, hence, he was guilty of offence punishable u/ss. 302 and 380 IPC.
holding: The conviction recorded by the Sessions Judge under sections 302/380/34 IPC is hereby converted to one u/ss. 302 and 380 IPC.
